about.title: Compton Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member changes everything, and the paperwork that follows can feel unbearable. In Compton, public records list 3 traffic deaths for 2025, alongside 333 injury collisions across streets like Compton Boulevard, Rosecrans Avenue, Alondra Boulevard and Wilmington Avenue. Each of those numbers represents a household that had to keep going without someone. A wrongful death claim under California law is a civil action, separate from any police investigation or criminal case, and it belongs to specific people: a spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The claim can seek funeral and burial costs, the income and support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Families generally have two years from the date of death, and far less if a Los Angeles County or city agency may share fault. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect you, at no charge, with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, so no fee is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Compton Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who is allowed to file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can sort out where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be brought within two years of the date of death, and a much shorter window applies when a government entity is involved. Getting connected sooner protects those dates.

items.title: Every category of loss accounted for
items.desc: Funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance are all recognized under California law. Contingency representation means no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My brother was killed in a crash on Rosecrans Avenue. Can I bring the wrongful death claim myself?
items.answer: It depends on who else survives him. California gives first priority to a spouse or domestic partner and children; siblings generally have standing only if none of those relatives exist or if they can show they depended on him financially. An independent attorney can review your family situation and explain exactly who may file.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, and it can move forward whether or not the district attorney files charges or wins a conviction. The criminal case is about punishment; the civil claim is about your family's losses, and the standards of proof are different.

items.question: What if a city or county vehicle or road condition played a role in the death?
items.answer: Claims against a public agency, including the City of Compton or Los Angeles County, follow a much shorter timeline than the usual two years, often measured in months. Missing that first administrative step can end the case before it begins. This is one of the main reasons families connect with an attorney quickly rather than waiting.
